cite: Section 35 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019
plain: Sets out how a complaint is made before the District Commission. A consumer can file it themselves; a lawyer is not required.
use_when: Telling the user they can file a complaint on their own.
source: https://nyaaya.org/?p=788 (secondary). Check bare act on India Code.

cite: Section 39 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019
plain: If the complaint is proved, the commission can order the defect to be removed, the goods replaced or the price refunded, and compensation paid.
use_when: Explaining what the commission can order.
source: https://nyaaya.org/?p=788 (secondary). Check bare act on India Code.

cite: Section 69 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019
plain: A complaint must be filed within two years from the date the problem (cause of action) arose.

cite: Section 69 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019
plain: A complaint filed after two years can still be accepted if the commission is satisfied there was sufficient cause for the delay.
use_when: Only when the case may be past the time limit.

act: Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021
plain: Complaints up to Rs 50 lakh go to the District Commission, above Rs 50 lakh up to Rs 2 crore to the State Commission, and above Rs 2 crore to the National Commission.
use_when: Explaining which commission hears the case.

cite: Rule 4(5) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
plain: The e-commerce platform's grievance officer must acknowledge a consumer complaint within 48 hours and resolve it within one month.
use_when: Explaining that the platform had a duty to respond.

cite: Section 34 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019
plain: A complaint can be filed in the district where the complainant lives or works.

cite: Section 2(10) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019
plain: Defines 'defect' as any fault, imperfection, or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity, or standard of goods.
source: Section 2(10) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019; verified via official bare act text.
